headline: Margins widen on biologics demand, cyber cost drag
summary_short: West Pharmaceutical Services reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $872.3M, up 13.8% y/y, as Proprietary Products net sales rose 16.6% on strong Biologics/GLP-1 and self-injection device demand; diluted EPS of $2.15 rose 18.1% y/y, while West Vantage profit fell on cyber-incident production downtime.
summary_long: Revenue rose 13.8% y/y to $872.3M (12.7% organic), driven by Proprietary Products' 16.6% growth as HVP components (+18.4% organic) gained from strong Biologics and GLP-1 demand and HVP delivery devices (+29.2% organic) rose on self-injection device demand. West Vantage grew just 2.0% as roughly $7M of revenue was lost to production downtime from the May 2026 cyber incident. Consolidated gross margin expanded 200bp to 37.7% on favorable HVP mix and pricing, partly offset by inflation. Diluted EPS rose 18.1% y/y to $2.15. Cash fell to $435.8M q/q after $156.7M of buybacks under the new $1B program; long-term debt held flat at $202.9M. No FY2026 guidance was given in this filing.

drivers.explanation: HVP components (+18.4% organic) grew on strong Biologics and GLP-1 demand and pricing; HVP delivery devices (+29.2%) rose on self-injection device demand.
200bp margin expansion to 37.7% driven by favorable HVP sales mix, including GLP-1 products, and price increases, partly offset by inflation and plant costs.
Growth tracked the gross-margin gain above; West Vantage operating profit fell on production inefficiencies tied to the May 2026 cyber incident, partially offsetting the increase.
Decline reflects $156.7M of share repurchases in the quarter under the new $1B buyback program and capital expenditures, partly offset by operating cash flow.

Proprietary Products (Biologics/GLP-1, self-injection devices) drove growth and margin expansion; West Vantage was held back by roughly $7M of cyber-incident-related downtime. No FY2026 guidance was reiterated or changed in the filing.
